chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah support him — informed me of, from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Qummī, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about a Muslim man who dies while traveling.

And there is no Muslim man with him, but there are Christian men with him, and his paternal aunt and maternal aunt, who are Muslim women, are with him — how should his ghusl be done? He عليه السلام said: “His paternal aunt and maternal aunt should wash him while he is in his shirt, and the Christians should not approach him.” And about a woman who dies while traveling, and there is no Muslim woman with her, but there are Christian women with them, and her paternal uncle and maternal uncle are with her and are Muslims, he said: “They should wash her, and the Christian woman must not approach her as though she were washing her, except that she should have a garment over her and water should be poured over the garment.” I said: If a Muslim man dies and there is no Muslim man with him, nor any Muslim woman from among his relatives, and there are Christian men with him and Muslim women between whom and him there is no kinship? He said: “The Christians should perform ghusl, then they should wash him, for necessity has arisen.” And about a Muslim woman who dies and there is no Muslim woman with her, nor a Muslim man from among her relatives, and there is with her a Christian woman and Muslim men, he said: “The Christian woman should perform ghusl, then wash her.”

The Shaykh — may Allah Most High support him — said: If a Muslim boy dies among Muslim women, with no blood relation between any one of them and him, and there is no man with them, and the boy is five years old, some of the women should wash him unclothed. But if he is more than five years old, they should wash him over his clothes, pouring water over him, not uncovering his private part, and bury him in his clothes after embalming him with what we have described. And if a young girl dies among Muslim men, with no mahram for her among them, and she is less than three years old, they should unclothe her and wash her. But if she is more than three years old, they should wash her in her clothes, pouring water over her, embalm her after the washing, and bury her in her clothes.

key_terms.اضْطُرَّ: necessity arose, allowing an exceptional ruling
key_terms.تَحْنِيطِهِ: embalming the deceased with the prescribed substances
key_terms.دِرْعٌ: a garment covering the body during washing
key_terms.ذَوِي قَرَابَتِهِ: his close relatives whose kinship affects eligibility
key_terms.عَوْرَةً: the private part that must not be uncovered
key_terms.غُسْلِهِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.قَمِيصِهِ: his shirt, indicating washing while clothed
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person with unmarriageable kinship affecting lawful handling

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be given ghusl in Islam when no eligible Muslim relative is present?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for washing the deceased in cases of travel, absence of same-sex Muslims, and situations of necessity. It addresses who may perform ghusl, when washing must be done over clothing, and special rulings for boys and girls based on age and kinship.
